title: Declare the page's annotation kit

blocks.text: The page declares its annotations with `@interface`, and its best practices say: **always state `@Retention` and `@Target`**, give optional elements meaningful defaults, use an enum rather than a `String` for a fixed set of choices, and add `@Documented` to public API annotations. The default retention is CLASS, which reflection cannot see.
`Kit` already names each annotation and its elements. Add the meta-annotations and defaults so that every one of them is readable at run time:

cases.says: ApiEndpoint is RUNTIME, targets methods, is @Documented, requires path and defaults method to GET, description to "" and version to 1.
ApiEndpoint.produces() defaults to the one-element array {"application/json"}.
Author is RUNTIME, has a single value() element for the shorthand, and targets exactly methods and types.
ThreadSafe has no elements, targets types and is RUNTIME, so reflection can see it.
Role is @Repeatable with Roles as its container, and Roles.value() returns Role[].
Auditable is @Inherited, targets types and defaults level to INFO.

concepts: Custom annotations come as markers, single-value, multi-value and repeatable annotations.
A custom annotation is declared with @interface; its elements look like methods, may have defaults, and a single element named value allows the shorthand @Author("Jane").
Without @Retention(RUNTIME) an annotation keeps the default CLASS retention and is invisible to reflection.
@Retention, @Target, @Documented, @Inherited and @Repeatable on an annotation type decide when it is kept, where it applies, whether Javadoc shows it and how it is inherited or repeated.
